subject: Post-demo: performance targets, streaming needs, and context ceiling impact
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina@opsloop.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: perf targets & streaming/context clarifications

Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the level of detail. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the perf POC properly: 

High-level requirements we captured:
- Latency: target p50 ~200ms for short/typical queries; streaming used for progressive response rendering.
- Concurrency: 800–1,200 concurrent active sessions expected at peak.
- Context: occasional single-session inputs up to ~30k tokens (mix of system + long user history + retrieval). Outputs typically 500–3,000 tokens, occasionally up to ~4k on summarization flows.
- Reliability: customer-facing agent must not exceed 2% error rate; graceful degradation required (fallback to smaller model or truncated context).
- Security: SOC2 + data retention controls; no PHI to be retained in logs without explicit consent.

Clarifying questions for you (Nina):
1) For streaming, do you require chunked tokens as they become available (client-side render) or is server-side fully-assembled responses acceptable for some flows?
2) Do you have any hard p95 latency targets for the interactive flows (we previously heard p50 targets but want an upper bound for capacity planning)?
3) Can you share a small set of representative payloads (one or two examples of the 30k token case and a 3k token output)? We listed a sample_app_payload.jsonl as an attachment stub — please replace with your canonical examples if preferred.

Next steps we propose:
- Redwood to provision a temporary Dedicated pool for a 2-week perf POC (config + canary routing) and run throughput/concurrency ramp tests.
- OpsLoop to provide sample payloads + any security checklist items we need for a POC (KMS, IP allowlist, retention windows).
- Meet again after we have baseline numbers (timeline: kick off this week, results within 10 business days).

I'll schedule a short sync with engineering and share a test plan draft. If any of the bullets above are off, flag them and we'll adjust.

Thanks,
Dev

--
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Nina Park <nina@opsloop.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Leo Chen <leo@opsloop.ai>
Date: 2026-10-18T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: perf targets & streaming/context clarifications

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Streaming: we do want token-by-token streaming for the agent UI so users see progressive replies. For long-generation jobs (reports) we can accept assembled responses, but interactive chat must stream.
- Latency: our product team would like p50 around 200ms for short prompts, p95 ideally < 600ms for interactive flows. For heavy 30k token queries we can accept p95 up to ~1.5s if streaming is active (since initial tokens should arrive sooner).
- Concurrency: 800 concurrent interactive users is our steady peak; we may see burst spikes to 1,200 for promos.
- Context behavior: those 30k token sessions are mostly a concatenation of retrieved docs + user history; we can trim older history if needed but prefer smart chunking vs outright truncation.
- Security: SOC2 attestation required for production deployment; for POC we can sign an NDA and provide a scoped dataset with PII redacted. Procurement (cc: Leo) will push PO/contract questions after we see POC numbers.

Attached one sample prompt (example_prompt.txt) representing a typical large retrieval-augmented query. I will follow up with a small zipped set of 5 payloads by EOD.

-Nina

On Oct 18, 2026, at 4:12 PM, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the demo today — appreciate the level of detail. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the perf POC properly:
> ...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo: perf targets & streaming/context clarifications

Thanks for the recap, Dev — good capture. Action items I recommend we split across Sales/Eng/Ops: 

Sales (Marissa)
- Confirm SOW boundaries and draft a short POC addendum that limits scope to performance testing and non-production data.
- Engage Procurement (we'll wait for Leo to provide PO windows) but draft standard POC terms.

Engineering (Karthik)
- Build a perf test plan that covers: steady-state concurrency 800, burst tests to 1,200, ramp to 2,000 qps for 5–10s windows to test autoscaling.
- Targets: aim for p50 180–250ms for short prompts; p95 <= 700ms for interactive flows when streaming is enabled. For 30k-token flows accept higher p95 but ensure first token latency in streaming < 400ms.
- Provide fallback policies: model-variant downgrade or truncation policy and an observable signal to surface to product if fallbacks occur.

Ops/Infra
- Prepare a temporary Dedicated pool (config proposal: start with 2 nodes, allow scaling to 6 for stress tests).
- Ensure KMS keys are available and add OpsLoop IP ranges to allowlist for the POC.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Dev: test-plan draft (48 hours) + sample job configs (sample_app_payload.jsonl placeholder).
- Karthik/Eng: perf test harness and expected metric dashboard (10 business days).
- Marissa/Sales: POC addendum + engage Procurement (Marissa) after baseline numbers.

I'll own the POC SOW doc and loop Procurement once Nina confirms the payloads. If anyone sees risk on the latency targets above, call it out now.

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Nina Park <nina@opsloop.ai>, Leo Chen <leo@opsloop.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T17:32:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: perf targets & streaming/context clarifications — POC next steps

Nina / Leo —
Following Marissa's note, we're set to kick off the perf POC once you share the sample payloads and confirm procurement timing. Attached are the items we'll use for the test harness: sample_app_payload.jsonl (placeholder — please replace with your canonical examples), example_prompt.txt (from your note), and a network_diagram.png showing the expected client topology.

Scheduling: I proposed a 30-minute sync in your calendar for tomorrow to confirm the dataset and access details. If that doesn't work, reply with a preferred time.

Quick checklist for OpsLoop to return so we can provision the Dedicated pool: 
- Sample payloads (5 files, representative of short & long contexts)
- IP ranges for allowlist + preferred KMS key alias
- Any retention/PII constraints for logs (POC vs production)
- Procurement contact & PO window (Leo cc'd)

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/OPSL-493) and shared Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cOpsLoopPerfPOC).

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.

Dev

--
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Key items: streaming required for interactive flows, p50 target ~200ms, p95 target <600-700ms for interactive flows (higher acceptable for 30k token jobs with streaming), concurrency steady 800 burst up to 1,200. Action: Redwood to provision Dedicated pool for 2-week perf POC; OpsLoop to provide sample payloads, IP ranges, and procurement timing. Deliverables and owners assigned with a 10 business day engineering run for metrics.
